title: Delhi Police grants Congress permission for November 1 rally at Ramlila Maidan

tea.why: Protesting against the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls and the actions of the Election Commission.
tea.want: Demanding the rollback of SIR and the use of ballot papers instead of EVMs.
tea.changed: Oct 17: Delhi Police issued a no-objection certificate to Congress for a November 1 rally at Ramlila Maidan.

summary: The Indian National Congress has received official clearance from the Delhi Police to hold a major public rally at Ramlila Maidan on November 1, 2026. The approval follows the de-notification of Jantar Mantar as a designated protest venue, leaving Ramlila Maidan, Burari Ground, and CBD Ground as the newly designated alternative sites in the capital. The upcoming demonstration is part of a broader series of protests organized by the opposition camp, including the INDIA bloc, centering on controversies regarding the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls and demands for elections to be conducted via ballot papers rather than electronic voting machines. Deputy Commissioner of Police Rohit Rajbir Singh confirmed that security and law-and-order arrangements are being coordinated with event organizers and municipal authorities.
demands: Rollback of the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls
Resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar
Conducting elections using ballot papers instead of EVMs
response: According to the Delhi Police, a No Objection Certificate (NOC) was issued to the Congress party for the November 1 rally after coordinating security arrangements and verifying venue availability with the Municipal Corporation of Delhi.

updates.text: The INDIA bloc finalized a joint action plan including rallies and save democracy marches over the SIR row.
Delhi Police issued a No Objection Certificate to Congress for a rally at Ramlila Maidan scheduled for November 1.
